newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber weakens in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber weakens in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices softened in late trading on Tuesday on sustained bearish market sentiment, traders said.
They said deals were done at 44.00 U.S. cents/lb fob Palembang and Padang for August shipment. Singapore dealers bought rubber at 44.50 for October shipment from the centres.
Traders offered August shipment SIR20 at 44.25 fob Surabaya, 44.50 fob Medan and 43.75 fob Pontianak and Jambi.
"Offer prices have fallen below 44.00 (in Pontianak and Jambi), which was thought to be the resistance level," said one trader.
"Maybe the best solution to improve this poor sentiment is intervention by INRO (the International Natural Rubber Organisation) so that prices will not continue to fall," he said.
Traders said INRO intervention, however, could not be effective if purchases only amounted to 10,000 tonnes.

"The intervention won't be effective if INRO buys between 10,000 and 20,000 tonnes and then stops. Moreover, I think the move may change the sentiment if the purchase is quite big...at least 50,000 tonnes," said one trader.
"If this happens, I think prices will bounce to 50.00 U.S. cents/lb," he added.
